Chapter - I
Agriculture and Allied Sector
Agriculture
Introduction:
Agriculture is the mainstay of the state economy. The overall contribution of the Agriculture and Allied
sector to the state GDP in 2020-21 was recorded as 19.2 percent. Almost 89 percent of the population of the
state is living in villages and agriculture and related sectors provide livelihood and employment to 76
percent of the population. Therefore development of agriculture is crucial for the overall development of
the state. The state government has been emphasizing on the development of the agriculture sector
through a comprehensive and holistic development approach which is commonly known as the Agriculture
Road Map.
Agriculture department has been implementing Agric ulture Roadmap since 2008 and as a
result we have witnessed many positive developments. Production and productivity have seen expected
growth. Two agriculture road maps have been already implemented and the third agriculture road map for
2017-2022 is curre ntly being implemented, and has been extended till 2023 after due approval from State
Cabinet. The implementation of the Agriculture Roadmap has brought several laudable achievements. The
state has received 5 Krishi Karman Puraskar for gains in production and productivity of Rice, Wheat and
Maize since 2012.
With the launch of 1st Agriculture Road Map in 2008, the state took a major

source_organization: Government of Bihar

d 5 Krishi Karman Puraskar for gains in production and productivity of Rice, Wheat and
Maize since 2012.
With the launch of 1st Agriculture Road Map in 2008, the state took a major step forward
for the holistic development of agriculture in the state. Plan outlay for agriculture has increased more than
100 times, from Rs. 20.43 crore in 2005-06 to Rs. 2781 crore during 2022-23.
Major achievements have been recorded in increasing the Seed Replacement Rate (SRR) of
Rice and Wheat. SRR for rice increased from 42.88 percent in 2016-17 to 49.35 percent in 2021-22. Similarly,
for Wheat it was around 20 percent in 2016 -17 and it is recorded as 44.17 percent in 2021 -22. Integrated
Seed Village Program is being implemented by Bihar Rajya Beej Nigam (BRBN) with an objective of seed
production. Under this scheme paddy, wheat, gram, tur and lentil Foundation seeds are being made
available at 50 percent subsidized rate. In addition to that BRBN buys back the seeds produced by the
farmers.
Climate change is a global issue and not only Bihar but the whole world have seen a
considerable threat and have been adversely affected by climate change. Irregularities in weather, flood,
drought, nutrition loss are few impacts of climate change which is adversely impacting the farmer's income.
Climate Resilient Agriculture Program has been adopted by the state to address this issue and to enable the
document_title: Bihar Annual Scheme 2022-23 - Agriculture and Allied Sector
source_organization: Government of Bihar

acts of climate change which is adversely impacting the farmer's income.
Climate Resilient Agriculture Program has been adopted by the state to address this issue and to enable the
farmers to adopt the practice of Changes in Crop Cycle and Agriculture Technology according to the change
in weather.
Farm mechanization has received a new boost with increased public support and farmer’s
keen interest in adoption of latest farm machinery like zero tillage, happy seeder, laser levellers etc. The
moribund agriculture extension system has been revived with inclusion of agriculture graduates in the
capacity of Agriculture Coordinator, Assistant Director etc. and farmers as Kisan Salahkar in the state.
Two Agriculture Road Maps have already been implemented and the Third Agriculture Road
Map for 2017-23 is now implemented in the state. The Third Agriculture Roadmap has been drawn with the
following objectives :
 To ensure Food Security.
 To foster Nutritional Security.
 To ensure increase in income of farmers to viable levels.
 To ensure farm agricultural growth with focus on gender and human aspects.

Strategy:
The following strategy would be adopted for the Annual Scheme 2022-23:
 Inputs: Production, availability at farmers’ accessible places, timeliness, cost and quality.
 Minimizing cost and maximising return: Promotion of technologies and management practices which
tend to decrease cost of cultivation and maximize return.
 Sustainable production system: Utilization of land, water and labour resources for best possible crop
mix to suit to the conditions arising out of the global climate change. Crop and Enterprise
diversification will be lead to sustainable production system. Recycling of organic w astes for use as
organic fertilizers.
 Extension: Transformation of agriculture information to knowledge and science into technology for
agriculture scientists, students, farmers and extension workers. Reorganisation of extension to make it
efficient, accountable and transparent.

1.10.4 Sugarcane
Inspite of availability of fertile lands and sufficient man power Agricultural development is stagnant due to
persistent natural calamities. Almost 2/3rd of cultivable land and 3/4 th of population has to face either flood
or drought every year resulting in loss of production and productivity. Sugarcane Crop can withstand flood
and drought upto some extent, hence has less impact on production in respect of cereal & pulse crops.
Development of Sugarcane and its by -products can contribute to growth of agricultural sector & rural
economy. At present Sugarcane productivity of Bihar is 49.75 MT/hectare and sugar recovery is 9.64 %. The
department aims at bringing the average productivity of the State of Bihar higher to the national average
productivity and simultaneously improve its recovery percentage from 9.64 % to 11.50 % during Krishi

Bihar is one of the important agricultural states in the
country with around 80% population engaged in
agriculture (more than the national average). It is one of
the leading producers of vegetables & fruits in India,
including many GI tagged crops. However, with very
minimal primary and secondary processing happening

processing, reduction of wastage, value addition and
promote exports, the State government has launched
Bihar Agri Investment Promotion Policy (BA-IPP) 2020.

Central and State sponsored programmes/schemes and

array of enabling programmes / schemes under
Atmanirbhar Bharat, which will give boost to the agri
